name: Nissan Skyline GT-R (R33)
h1: Nissan Skyline GT-R R33 (BCNR33): specs, RB26 engine and what owners say

us.x: Never sold new in the US. R33 GT-Rs became legal to import under the 25-year rule from January 2020, each car once it is 25 years old by its month of build.

films.x: Leon, one of Dom’s crew, drives a bright yellow R33 GT-R. The film car started out white with black graphics, and years later it was seized and crushed in a VIN-tampering case.

RB26DETT.name: Nissan RB26DETT
facts: Inline-6, DOHC 24-valve, iron block, aluminum head, belt-driven cams
280 PS (276 hp) at 6,800 rpm, 368 Nm (271 lb-ft) at 4,400 rpm in the R33
Two turbos in parallel with ceramic turbine wheels; the R34 got ball-bearing units
Six individual throttle bodies instead of one

issues.x: The stock turbos have ceramic turbine wheels, which Wikipedia says are weak at high boost. PistonHeads warns that overspinning a turbo can break the wheel off its shaft, and that a noisy turbo points to worn bearings.

PistonHeads says crankcase pressure can push oil past the turbos into the intake, and too much oil in the head can starve the sump and spin a bearing. It says to change the oil at least every 6,000 miles.
PistonHeads lists failing coil packs as an R34 weak spot, and names plugs, coil packs and airflow meters as the usual causes of poor running on the R33.
